_comment: What a block may be as an Age's rock or ground, for a word asking for one by what it is like:
`"stone": "#frozen"`. Every block a world can be made of is read; only one some rule speaks to is
`by_kind` is the half that survives offline: `lit` is a block that gives light. Map colours are not read
(Jonah, 2026-09-29) -- they are the roughest guess at how a block looks and say nothing about what it is
like; `dark` and `bright` are hand-tagged in preset_tags/materials.json instead.
`withheld_from_broad_words` is the fence (Jonah, 2026-09-29): a block in any of these tags is never
drawn by a query, however well it answers one. A world of blue ice or of diamond is reached by
learning its word. The two ink tags are our own statement of what a block is worth -- a word for one
needs fine or masterwork ink, so a broad word handing it out would walk round the ink -- and they are
read from their files offline, so the fence is the same with or without a server. The last two catch
what a mod adds, where tags are bound.
